gaps.lead: I always hated pasta when I was a child, but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.sentence: I ___ pasta when I was a child but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.explanation: 'used to + infinitive' describes a past state or habit that is no longer true.

gaps.lead: The doctor said that he should take a complete rest.
gaps.sentence: The doctor advised ___ a complete rest.
gaps.explanation: say + should → advise + object + to-infinitive: advised him to take.

gaps.lead: My grandfather planted all these apple trees himself.
gaps.sentence: My grandfather is the ___ all these apple trees.
gaps.explanation: 'the one who…' identifies the agent with a relative clause.

gaps.lead: She'll be on a flight, so she can't join the call.
gaps.sentence: She'll be on a flight, so ___ join the call.
gaps.explanation: won't be able to = future inability.

gaps.lead: We packed a spare tyre because the road might be bad.
gaps.sentence: We packed a spare tyre ___ bad.
gaps.hint: in case = because it might happen
gaps.explanation: in case + clause = as a precaution against a possibility.

gaps.lead: It would be sensible to leave before the traffic builds up.
gaps.sentence: We ___ before the traffic builds up.
gaps.explanation: 'It would be sensible to do' = 'we had better do' — had better + bare infinitive.
